summary: The difference between how things are today and how they should be.
example: Today the depot finds one fault in five and buyers find the rest. The aim is for the depot to find most faults, before produce leaves.
definition: A shortfall in results: the distance between a current state (what is) and a desired state (what should be), measured against the purpose and the goals above it (Kaufman's needs assessment). A need is a gap in results, not in resources or methods, and it is named as a noun, not a verb. A gap closes into one or more outcomes, named on the gap's side, since a goal never points below itself. Where a KPI measures it, the KPI's dated baseline and target are its two states and are not restated. It lists the segments it was observed in, so work that cites it can say which part it addresses and the register can show which part nobody is working on. It is written once in the gap register and cited by the problems of the projects and programmes that address it. A gap is not a problem (what the shortfall does to a named group, on one piece of work, which cites the gap), not an outcome (the state that will be true once it closes), not a missing resource or a method (no scanners, train the staff), and not a KPI (the measure it may be read on).

/metadata/name.guide: A few words naming the shortfall as a reader would scan it in the register: a noun phrase or a short statement of what is wrong, never the work that would fix it.

poor.why: A verb and a method: it names the remedy, not the shortfall in results.
A topic, not a shortfall: it says neither what is wrong nor where.
A gap in resources, not in results: say what the missing scanners cause, such as faults found after dispatch.

/spec/measure.guide: The KPI whose baseline and target already are this gap's two states, when one tracks it. Choose it first: with a measure, the current and desired states are read from the KPI and need not be written. Leave it empty when no KPI tracks the shortfall yet; the gap is then an observation, and that is said, not hidden with an invented number.
good: post-harvest-loss-rate, for the gap Too much harvest is lost after picking: its baseline of 18 percent is where things are, its target of 9 percent is where they should be.

poor.text: member-season-earnings, for the gap Faults are found after dispatch
poor.why: Earnings move for many reasons; the measure of a gap is the KPI whose baseline and target are this shortfall's two states, not one it might eventually touch.

poor.text: quality-pass-rate, while also writing 62 and 75 into the current and desired states
poor.why: The numbers then live in two places and can come to disagree; with a measure, the KPI holds them.

/spec/current.guide: Where things are now, in one short sentence, as a result someone could observe: the what is half of the gap. When a KPI measures the gap, its baseline is the current state and this may be left empty.
good: One fault in five is found at intake; buyers find the rest.
Each depot checks against its own checklist.

poor.why: Too vague to tell when it has changed: say what is observed, and where.

poor.text: Depots lack trained staff and scanners.
poor.why: Missing means, not a result: say the result they produce, such as faults reaching buyers.

/spec/desired.guide: Where things should be, in one short sentence, as a state that will be true: the what should be half. It may be an ideal that a dated target approaches over several periods. When a KPI measures the gap, its target is the desired state.
good: Most faults are found at intake, before produce leaves the depot.
Every depot checks against one published standard.

poor.text: Train every depot supervisor in the standard.
poor.why: An action, which is a method: say the result that would be true once the training worked.
Says nothing a reader can check: state the result itself.

/spec/outcomes.guide: The outcome or outcomes that would be true once this gap is closed: where the desired state is reached. Outcome-level goals only. This is how the gap connects to the strategy above it; one outcome can close several gaps. When no outcome fits, define it first under its objective.
good: faults-found-before-dispatch, for the gap Faults are found after dispatch
depot-staff-apply-the-standard-alike, for the gap No single quality standard

poor.why: A goal, not an outcome: a gap closes into a changed state, which sits two levels below it.
An objective, an aim to act on; name the outcome under it that says what will be true.

/spec/segments.guide: The slices the shortfall was observed in, as declared Segments: the parts the evidence covers, at the level work will be divided by, so a project can address one of them and be recorded as addressing that part and no more. Name the values (the northern region, the southern region), not only the dimension. These say where the shortfall was observed; who the work is for belongs to the problem's beneficiary groups.
good: northern-region and southern-region, for a review that found faults reaching buyers in both
fresh-produce and dried-produce, as values of product-line

poor.why: Only the dimension: work could then claim every region or none. Name the regions the evidence covers.
A beneficiary group, a group of people the work is for, not a slice the shortfall was observed in.

/spec/source.guide: Where the finding was written down, precisely enough that someone else could find the page: the document and its section. Provenance, not a link.
good: Quality review of the 2025 spring season, section 2
Quality review of the 2025 spring season, section 4

poor.why: Not precise enough to find again: which season, which section?
A role, not a record: name the document that holds what they reported.

/spec/statement.guide: The finding in the source's own words, quoted as written. Never edited to fit the register: where a quote covers more than one segment, the quote stands and the segments carry the precision.
good: Four in five quality faults are found by a buyer rather than at intake.
Each depot keeps its own checklist and none of them agree.

poor.why: A recommendation, not the finding, and not the source's words.

poor.text: Four in five quality faults in the northern region are found by a buyer.
poor.why: The quote was edited to fit one segment; quote it as written and name the segment in Segments.

/spec/note.guide: Anything the quote cannot carry without ceasing to be the source's own words: how it was counted, or why it cannot be watched yet.
good: Counted by hand during the review; no system holds the checklists, so this cannot be watched yet.

poor.text: The quality check rollout is fixing this.
poor.why: Work addressing the gap is recorded on the work's side, where its problem cites the gap, so the register can count it.

/spec/dataSources.guide: Every data source this gap can be watched in, when it can be: name each one the evidence comes from, since a finding is often read from several at once. Leave it empty for a finding nothing records live.

Project:/spec/summary/problems/-/gaps/-/.ask: Which project addresses this gap, and which of its segments does that work reach? The project's problem cites the gap and names the segments; it names none only when it reaches the whole gap.
Project:/spec/summary/problems/-/gaps/-/.ifNone: Nothing has to be defined first: a gap nobody addresses is the finding a register exists to show. When a project takes it on, its problem cites this gap and names the segments it reaches.

Programme:/spec/problems/-/gaps/-/gap.ask: Which programme answers this gap, and which of its segments does it reach? The programme's problem cites the gap and names the segments; it names none only when it answers the whole gap.
Programme:/spec/problems/-/gaps/-/gap.ifNone: Nothing has to be defined first: leave the gap unaddressed and the check says so. When a programme takes it on, its problem cites this gap and names the segments it reaches.

checks.gap-states: State both the current and the desired state, or choose the KPI whose baseline and target are them.
checks.gap-outcome: Name the outcome that would be true once the gap is closed, defining it under its objective first if there is none.
checks.gap-measured: Choose the KPI that tracks this shortfall, or leave the gap as an observation until one exists.
checks.gap-source: Name the document and section the finding was written down in.
checks.gap-segments: Name the segments the evidence covers, as values rather than only their dimension.
checks.gap-covered: Have the work that addresses this gap cite it and name the segments it reaches, so no segment is left with nobody and no citation hides one by claiming the whole.
checks.gap-results: Say which result falls short, not which resource or method is missing.

good.label: a result that falls short of where it should be

poor.label: a missing resource, tool, budget or method

gap-results.fail: Reads as a missing resource or method: say which result falls short, and by how much.
